verdict.rationale: Shared payment tokens are documented as scoped grants to a specific seller. The issuer sets usage_limits (currency, max_amount, expires_at), can revoke the token at any time, and gets webhooks on each state change. Link CLI adds human-approved, one-time-use credentials (virtual cards or SPTs) for a specific spend request, so the agent never handles the real card number. The open-source repo and npm package corroborate that the CLI ships. Missing for 10: merchant restriction is only implied by the per-seller grant (and the Link virtual-card option explicitly works at any merchant), no hands-on or independent verification that limits are enforced, and parts of ACS are private preview or waitlist-gated.
